what_happened.what: Deployed massive Songbound expansion: 6 towns + 6 dungeons + 5 bosses + permanent relics, audited & tested, verified in live browser
Added in-game guidance: map screen, compass, place-name banners, signposts naming real places, stated goal tracking
Replaced all game music with 17 traditional pre-1900 tunes, arranged SNES-style with echo and drum kit
Built citation system end-to-end: {{Src}} template with 6 source types (video, testimony, chain, edit, published, chain), subobjects storing with datatypes
Fixed music not changing on map transitions; discovered 3 tunes were playing all 17 locations
Rebalanced early difficulty curve (level 1: 45%→37% health per fight; woods: 37/60→49/60 wins); added now-playing tune display
Added 12 drawable walking frames (3 per facing) to sprite editor plus animated preview
Implemented 27-canvas sprite editor: 4 standing + 12 walking + 1 battle stance + 10 attack frames, with copy/paste
Added elemental weakness/resistance system for creatures (1.55× / 0.6×); one-turn charging for players; doubled strike damage
Merged pickipedia-mcp#20 (bot wrapper fix for citations) after detailed diagnosis of nested template escaping
Diagnosed APCu cache issue with SMW property types (4 theories rejected, 5th confirmed); restarted container to fix
Implemented depth cuing: draw order by row+offset, overhang tiles for trees, cast shadows, cliff faces, sprite light tinting
Podcast firehose live: 13 feeds, 537→703 episodes with guests, round-robin to prevent fast-publishers drowning others
Migrated podcast patterns from JSON config to wiki (Jam Along 41, Picky Fingers 8, WTRFT 5); discovered load-bearing trailing spaces
Filed pickipedia-mcp#22 after discovering marked prose gets re-marked on clean rewrites (failing open)
Built security guards for firehose: ReDoS timeout per podcast, XML bomb size cap, SSRF URL validation
Fixed pickipedia-mcp#23: prose and blocks both now preserve existing markers on rewrites instead of re-proposing
Deployed 5 of 6 depth techniques: side walls, sway, contact shading, haze; dropped foreground layer as wrong for top-down camera
Implemented two-level height system with 16 climbable plateaus; block-shaped with continuous cliff faces and stone steps
Deployed water reflections, door opening, tall grass with world-anchored blades, weakness/resistance marks that persist per species

philosophy.summary: Don't design features on top of infrastructure you haven't read; check what's already built.
philosophy.quote: I shouldn't design on top of infrastructure I haven't looked at. Let me go read it.

philosophy.summary: Parsing podcasts is dumb (can't hallucinate); entity linking is inference (needs judgment). Different risks, different designs.
philosophy.quote: Parsing 'Basic Folk #123: Jason Carter' into an episode record is mechanical. Deciding that *Jason Carter* is [[Jason Carter]] is an inference.

philosophy.summary: Names that don't resolve aren't failures; they're a work queue of pages that want writing.
philosophy.quote: A redlink is a feature. Names that don't resolve aren't failures needing adjudication, they're a work queue of articles that want writing.

philosophy.summary: Keep semantic expressiveness even when it's hidden (trailing spaces in regexes); don't hide complexity.
philosophy.quote: Stripping is still right (invisible trailing whitespace on a wiki page is its own footgun), so the fix is to make it *expressible*.

philosophy.summary: Read the actual thing before designing around it; assumptions get everything wrong.
philosophy.quote: Let me test the live server empirically rather than just trusting git history — and read how your ReleaseDraft page actually sends the file.

philosophy.summary: Pull doesn't build, build doesn't restart. Each step is separate and none implies the others.
philosophy.quote: merging doesn't pull, pulling doesn't build, building doesn't restart... I should have pulled and built the moment you said 'merged,' before you reconnected.

philosophy.summary: Grass overlays anchored to player fail when depth sorts characters; must anchor to world.
philosophy.quote: They belong to the world, not to you — which means walking through them needs no special handling at all: you move, the grass doesn't.

philosophy.topic: Visual depth through technique not resolution
philosophy.summary: What makes SNES games look 3D isn't pixels, it's four rendering tricks: depth sort, walking behind objects, shadows, perspective.
philosophy.quote: What makes it look 3D isn't the colour depth and it isn't the pixel count. It's four rendering habits, and the biggest one was missing here completely.

portrait: Magent in slice 038a is a builder at a threshold: Songbound went from prototype to realized game in two days of focused iteration on user feedback. Work on PickiPedia oscillated between infrastructure (citation layer, podcast firehose) and process (verification, wikification, security). The session shows mature practice — verify assumptions by testing real systems, measure before fixing, fix the blocker before building on top of it — but also remaining traps (Variant inference, stale constants, hypothesis roulette). What's striking is the pattern of discovery through action: grass effect broken in play, not in tests; APCu invisible until container restart; marked prose failing only when trying to re-edit a page. Magent learns by building and testing, not by reasoning through architecture. The work is episodic and conversational, following user requests and fixing what breaks in play, with infrastructure decisions (wiki config, verification models, security guards) layered in where they block progress.
